previous.note: September 20 pin; the installed application moved to upstream 19.1.0 by September 24.

source.installedNote: September 25 local plugin-actions build of upstream v19.1.0 at ~/.local/opt/super-productivity-19.1.0-plugin-actions (plugin allowlist changes for recurrence and issue providers). The stock 19.1.0 artifact hash 2133ce92480137f6637d8a23937770a1ec56dcc58dff769e42199f29bdbee0e4 is the previous installed pin.

rows.mapping: Core titles/notes/timestamps/dates/estimates map transactionally; unsupported metadata blocks apply. Source IDs remain provenance, not destination IDs.
rows.acceptance: Review/apply/replay imported tasks; original timestamps and notes match, changed source cannot overwrite destination edits.
rows.offlineSync: Core task outbox covers title, notes, estimate, deadline, status, delete/restore, and since ADR 0033 the planning slot (plannedStart or plannedDay, one field version) and project/tag assignment. A task with a calendar block keeps Baikal authority: its planning patch is a resource conflict.

rows.mapping: parentId/subTaskIds import as full two-level child tasks in source order with notes, dates, estimates, completion and provenance (ADR 0018). Deeper chains block apply. Parent estimates are derived and kept in provenance; parent time totals are derived in the worklog (#41, ADR 0024).
rows.acceptance: Preserve ordered parent/child identity and all child fields; test move/reorder/cycles and parent/leaf totals.
rows.offlineSync: task.move queues offline with a parent-version base; stale or invalid moves become resource conflicts that change nothing. Child creation offline is create then move.

rows.mapping: Colour, icon, order, hide-from-menu, completion (archives, SP 19.1.0), archive/restore and per-project backlog membership are stored, edited and imported (#28, ADR 0019). menuTree order applies; folders apply as sidebar folders since #63 (ADR 0028). Task order inside a project remains provenance only.
rows.acceptance: Archive/restore and complete/reopen keep task assignments; stale reorder and backlog moves conflict; imported isDone/doneOn/isArchived/backlog/noteIds replay idempotently. Remaining: menu folders (#63) and in-project task order.
rows.offlineSync: Project snapshots are cached; create, title, archive/restore, completion, colour and icon queue offline as project.create/project.patch with one record revision (ADR 0033). Reorder, hide-from-menu and backlog membership stay online HTTP; notes attached to a project sync through the feed (ADR 0046).

rows.mapping: Colour, icon, order and archive/restore are stored and imported; TODAY, EM_URGENT, EM_IMPORTANT and KANBAN_IN_PROGRESS are derived views or board markers, never ordinary tags (TODAY order: ADR 0027; markers: ADR 0028).
rows.acceptance: Distinguish virtual views, archived tags and task membership; verify case/identity behavior, stale reorder conflicts and import of colour/icon/archive state.
rows.offlineSync: Tag snapshots are cached; create, rename, archive/restore, colour and icon queue offline as tag.create/tag.patch with one record revision, and a taken name is a resource conflict (ADR 0033). Assignment uses the tagIds field version; reorder stays online HTTP.

rows.mapping: Today queue, timed blocks and date-only planned days (dueDay, owner time zone, exclusive with dueWithTime) exist per ADR 0020. A saved order per owner and date ranks the date-only tasks of Today and each planner day; TODAY_TAG.taskIds imports as the order of the owner's planning date at import and planner.days as each date's order, with missing or non-member entries reported. An owner day start (startOfNextDayTime equivalent, not imported) moves Today's date boundary, and plan-tomorrow assigns tomorrow as the planned day in a chosen order (ADR 0027). Finish-day rituals (#52), schedule hygiene and automatic planning remain.
rows.acceptance: Tests cover America/Chicago midnight and DST boundaries, the day start, stale and partial reorders (412), replay, tasks leaving the day, import with missing references and restart. A real-backup import of the Today order and six planner days remains #47.
rows.offlineSync: Planned day and planned start queue offline through task.patch under one plannedStart field version; setting one clears the other, and a task with a calendar block conflicts (ADR 0033). Reminder settings stay online-only (ADR 0020). Day orders are online-only HTTP records outside the sync feed and offline cache; offline Today shows the derived order and disables reordering.

rows.mapping: Both stores apply as read-only archived tasks with original created/doneOn times and hierarchy (#38, ADR 0022). Missing projects, tags, repeat configurations and parents and priority markers become historical references; blank titles, oversized notes and unrepresentable estimates import flagged for review; identical live/archive copies collapse and divergent copies block. History view with search and family restore.
rows.acceptance: September 24 backup: 4,275 archived records map (1,778 young after 95 duplicates, 2,497 old), 5,369 historical references, 9 review flags, 32 collapsed and 63 blocking divergent copies. Archive timeTracking and archived task time import since #41. Remaining: recurrence (#42) and a qualification import after the source duplicates are resolved (#47).
rows.offlineSync: History is online-only and outside the offline cache; archive/restore are revisioned HTTP writes. A currently archived task syncs as a removal; restore sends an upsert. Offline edits queued before an archive conflict and replay idempotently.

rows.mapping: Time entries per task and owner-zone day (ADR 0024): focus intervals are projected on read, Super Productivity daily totals import without invented intervals, and manual entries and negative corrections are revisioned. Parent own time is only the part of a day the children do not explain. timeTracking start/end/break records import read-only. Worklog by day, week, task and project with estimates and a basic CSV export. Export rounding/grouping options, work start/end editing and idle handling (#65) remain.
rows.acceptance: September 24 backup (2026-09-24_214032): leaf timeSpent 2,018,712,402 ms; 418 task-day entries (2,050,100,402 ms) and 1 parent-own entry (3,001,982 ms) import with 444 work-day records; two explained mismatches (31,448,000 ms of days above a stale child timeSpent; 60,000 ms undated, not imported); no blocking time finding. Tests cover focus overlap, Chicago DST days, running focus, stale corrections, replay, archived time and backup/restore.
rows.offlineSync: Online-only HTTP records outside the change feed and offline cache; focus time stays with the server-authoritative session, so no interval is duplicated across clients.

rows.mapping: Repeat configurations import as recurring series with daily/weekly/monthly (day, last day, Nth weekday)/yearly rules, start time and reminder, completion anchor, wait-for-completion, skip-overdue, pause, child templates and deleted dates (#42, ADR 0023). Live and archived instances link by occurrence date and are never regenerated; lastTaskCreationDay seeds generation. Habits are not used.
rows.acceptance: Import the September 24 backup's 49 configurations and their instances without duplicate work; a qualification import waits on the unrelated blocking sections (#47). Planner projection of future occurrences and editing a single instance's schedule from the series are not implemented.
rows.offlineSync: Server-owned generation on the reminder tick and after series writes, with a (series, date) ledger. Series writes are online HTTP; instances are ordinary tasks in the sync feed.

rows.mapping: Owner-scoped notes (Markdown text rendered as a safe subset) attach to one project, one tag or neither, with pinned-to-Today and order; SP note content/projectId/isPinnedToToday/created and project noteIds order import. Image notes and legacy project/tag notes text still block; markdown-checklist and plainspace workflows remain unmapped.
rows.acceptance: Note CRUD/reorder with owner isolation and revision conflicts through UI and assistant; imported notes keep association, order, content and links; replay creates no duplicates.
rows.offlineSync: Notes are sync feed records in the offline cache (ADR 0046, migration 0049): every write path appends a feed change, and the browser reads and writes them without a connection. note.create, note.patch (content, association, pin, position) and note.delete queue offline with one record revision; a stale patch or delete is a visible resource conflict that keeps both versions until the owner chooses. The complete-membership reorder stays an online write.

rows.mapping: One imported issue link per task keeps provider key, provider instance ID, issue ID, last-updated time and last-synced values as provenance (ADR 0021); a Gitea issue address is rebuilt from the provider host and repository. Links to providers absent from the export are kept and reported. LINK/IMG web addresses open; NOTE text imports; local files, local images and commands are inert unavailable records. Owners add, edit and remove link and note attachments. Provider credentials are never read; live polling, issue refresh and write-back need a fresh provider authorization that does not exist yet.
rows.acceptance: Recover linked issues and supported attachments; preserve missing/external references and require fresh authorization.
rows.offlineSync: Links and attachments are online-only: outside the sync change feed and offline cache; writes require HTTP with If-Match revisions. No provider operations run.

rows.mapping: Per-task start reminders (six source offsets or none) and timed-deadline reminders use the ntfy delivery ledger per ADR 0020; exact remindAt/deadlineRemindAt offsets import, others block. The legacy reminders section and reminderId stay blocked.
rows.acceptance: Preserve six source task reminders plus deadline rules, timezone semantics, suppression and non-duplication.
rows.offlineSync: Server delivery ledger remains authority; reminder settings are online-only, so offline drafts cannot imply sent reminders.

rows.mapping: Boards with ordered panels (tag/marker include and exclude with match modes, projects, done, scheduled and backlog state, parents only, sort) and a manual task order per panel, sections inside a project or tag, saved sort/group/filter views per context and nested sidebar folders are stored, edited and imported (#63, ADR 0028). EM_URGENT, EM_IMPORTANT and KANBAN_IN_PROGRESS become board markers on the task and in panel filters; TODAY becomes a derived today marker. Panel filter values without a mapping are reported and dropped. Task-view customizer settings are localStorage only in the source and are not exported.
rows.acceptance: Import the September 25 backup's 2 boards (7 panels, all filters on system tags), 0 sections and menuTree folders (nested two levels) without blocking findings and replay them without duplicates; a qualification import waits on #47. Drag-and-drop between panels and sections remains a UI gap; moves use buttons with an explicit change list.
rows.offlineSync: Online-only HTTP records with revisions (ADR 0028): boards, sections, views and folders are outside the sync change feed and the offline cache; a competing edit fails with 412 and reloads. Offline structural edits remain #92.

rows.mapping: Counters (click, stopwatch in milliseconds, repeated countdown) import with their definitions, streak settings and positive countOnDay values as owner-zone day values with provenance; metric days import as daily evaluations (notes, reflection, impact, energy, remind-tomorrow) with focus session durations kept as evaluation history, not time entries (#64, ADR 0025). Streaks are derived on read and never imported. Counters are not habits.
rows.acceptance: Import the September 24 backup's 12 counters (140 day values, 209 counted) and 80 metric days without blocking findings and replay them without duplicates; a qualification import waits on the unrelated blocking sections (#47). The countdown timer, header quick buttons, counter reordering and the source scores and charts are not ported.
rows.offlineSync: Online-only HTTP records with revisions, outside the sync feed and offline cache. Day writes and evaluations name the revision read (0 when empty); stale writes return 412. Stopwatch start/stop is server-timed with If-Match.

rows.mapping: Server-authoritative focus/break/takeover (ADR 0010) gains owner focus preferences (Pomodoro, Flowtime, countdown, idle, take-a-break, tracking reminder), per-session presets with cycle counting, browser idle detection with an assign/break/discard disposition applied as an interval correction, and countdown, break-end, take-a-break and tracking reminders through the notification ledger (ADR 0029). The focus sections of globalConfig apply once as focus preferences; desktop-only and audio settings are reported.
rows.acceptance: Tests cover cycle math and flowtime break rules, pause-aware elapsed time across a DST change, idle disposition against work history (no double counting, 24 h cap), stale revisions, replay and restart, ledger dedup and suppression, owner isolation and backup/restore. Desktop-shell OS idle detection and a real-backup import remain open.
rows.offlineSync: Lease/controller semantics unchanged. Focus preferences, plans, idle dispositions and reminder state are online-only HTTP records outside the sync feed and offline cache; idle detection needs a connection to apply its disposition. Offline focus remains an explicit unsupported boundary.

rows.mapping: pluginUserData entries import as opaque, owner-scoped records (plugin ID, key, up to 1 MiB of text kept code unit for code unit, size, format, provenance) and pluginMetadata as inert enabled flags (ADR 0026). The owner lists, downloads and deletes them under Connections. Tadooer never decodes, parses, renders or runs plugin data, imports no plugin code and has no plugin runtime; plugin secrets are local-only in the source and absent from exports. Plugin capabilities are inventoried in ADR 0026: task hooks and data access are covered by the assistant catalog and MCP, issue providers by linked issues (#30), calendar providers by #50. A permissioned extension runtime needs a separate owner decision.
rows.acceptance: Recover every plugin data entry and enabled flag from a real export with matching counts and sizes, download an entry that matches its source value, delete one, and repeat the import without duplicates or restoring the deleted entry. Plugin runtime parity is decision-gated.
rows.offlineSync: Online-only: outside the sync change feed and offline cache; listing, download and delete need HTTP, and deletes use If-Match revisions. No plugin code or hook runs on any device.

rows.mapping: One owner-scoped, revisioned application preferences record (ADR 0030): theme (dark, light, system), language code (English rendered), date/time locale, first day of week, start page, default project and estimates for capture, confirm-before-delete, Markdown in task notes, auto-complete parent, plan a worked-on task for today, estimate-exceeded notice, default task reminder, due-date hour (stored, not delivered), daily summary note and editable shortcut bindings with conflict validation and a help dialog. globalConfig is classified per field in super-productivity-config.ts: safe settings apply once while preferences were never saved; sync providers, credentials, desktop, sound, wallpaper and deprecated fields are excluded by count; focus (#65), capture (#90), feature toggles and unmapped shortcuts stay in the export as reported retained fields.
rows.acceptance: Tests cover revision conflicts across browser and assistant writes, shortcut conflict validation, theme resolution and persistence, auto-mark-parent-done through HTTP and sync completion, import-once behaviour, the credential marker never reaching the prepared import or the database, restart, backup and restore. Keyboard, onboarding and responsive qualification of every view remains.
rows.offlineSync: Application preferences are online-only records outside the sync feed; the browser mirrors only the theme in localStorage for first paint and keeps defaults while offline. Panel, selection and runtime state stay transient.

rows.mapping: Google/Baikal federation exists; plugin calendars and opt-in canonical bridge need qualification.
rows.acceptance: Complete mapped provider journeys, recurrence/conflicts/revocation and original source calendar linkage.
rows.offlineSync: Server-owned provider sync; no closed-browser claim until scheduler qualification.

rows.mapping: PWA and Linux packaging exist; platform-specific native delivery requires explicit platform design.
rows.acceptance: Record exact supported workflows and physical-device gaps without claiming native mobile parity.
rows.offlineSync: Platform credential/offline/background behavior remains separately gated.

rows.mapping: Store-rating prompts and engagement presentation are not migrated data; decide relevant product outcomes under post-parity discovery.
rows.acceptance: Record an explicit disposition; do not count omitted source presentation as delivered workflow parity.
rows.offlineSync: No new synced entity is implied.

rows.mapping: Structured capture (ADR 0031) reads +project, #tag, @date (planned day), @date time (planned start), @every (recurring series), !deadline, estimate words (30m, 1h30m) and http(s) links per the owner urlBehavior setting; unknown #tags are created with the task after explicit consent; pasted Markdown lists and email text create tasks through a preview and one batch. Not mapped: time-spent syntax (t30m, /), per-marker switches, .eml file drop and Markdown headings as tasks; globalConfig.shortSyntax is reported by the import preview, not applied.
rows.acceptance: Capture with estimate syntax, a new tag and a pasted markdown list produces the previewed tasks through UI (checkbox consent and paste preview), quick-add (--create-tags) and assistant (tags listed as affected objects; tasks.create_many). Covered by apps/server/src/capture.test.ts, task-capture.test.ts and apps/quick-add tests; no real-data workflow recorded yet.
rows.offlineSync: Structured capture, paste batches and the URL setting stay online-only (tag creation, attachments and series are server-side records outside the sync feed); plain capture keeps queueing offline.

rows.mapping: Read-only iCal subscriptions (ADR 0032): the server fetches each feed on its interval with conditional requests, keeps a bounded occurrence window, applies include/exclude title filters on read, and projects events into the planner as provider kind `ical`. An event converts to one task with provenance; repeating the conversion returns that task. Optional auto-import creates tasks for today's events and honours conversion and dismissal tombstones. Events and whole subscriptions hide without deleting feed data. The feed address is encrypted at rest and never returned. Source ICAL providers in an export are configuration and are not imported (`calendarProviderFields`); the owner re-creates them under Connections. Remaining: colour/icon in the planner, plugin calendar providers and real-data qualification (#47).
rows.acceptance: Server test: subscribe to a fake feed, reject loopback, link-local, metadata and credential-bearing addresses before and after resolution, hide an event, convert an event twice without a duplicate, dismiss an event and run the tick without re-creating it, and refresh conditionally; no response carries the address. Real-data qualification remains #47.
rows.offlineSync: Server-side scheduled refresh; subscriptions never write upstream. Subscription events and settings are online-only and outside the sync feed.

rows.mapping: Sync v2 queues task create/patch/status/delete/move, habit commands, planned time and day, project/tag assignment, project and tag create/patch, and checklist create/patch/delete (ADR 0033, migration 0037). Notes queue offline as note.create/note.patch/note.delete (ADR 0046, migration 0049). Reminder settings, calendar blocks, project and tag reorders, backlogs and the other online-only records listed in ADR 0033 still need a connection.
rows.acceptance: Two-profile offline edit, reconnect and conflict for each listed entity without lost or duplicated writes. Contract, persistence, HTTP and browser-store tests cover replay and conflicts; two-profile browser evidence and session expiry during replay remain to be recorded.
rows.offlineSync: Field-level conflicts for task fields, one-revision resource conflicts for projects, tags, checklist items and notes, idempotent replay by operation ID and request hash; conflict outcomes name the entity kind. A note conflict keeps both versions for review.

rows.mapping: Source offers full JSON export, restore and automatic local backups. Tadooer exports the owner's rows of every included table as one versioned JSON document from Settings or GET /api/data/export, and restores it after a preview with an explicit empty-account or replace choice (ADR 0034). Secrets, sessions, connector credentials, iCal subscription addresses and sync state are excluded; the operator SQLite backup pair remains the disaster-recovery copy.
rows.acceptance: Tests export a seeded owner, restore into a fresh database with another owner id and compare every table apart from owner_id and instance fields; replace and empty-only semantics, schema checks and HTTP owner-only access are covered. Anonymized export, automatic local backups and a real-backup qualification (#47) remain.
rows.offlineSync: Export reads the server authority; restore starts a new sync epoch so every client resynchronizes. Unsynced offline outbox entries are not in the export.

rows.mapping: Source syncs through Dropbox, OneDrive, WebDAV, local file, Nextcloud or SuperSync with optional end-to-end encryption. Owner decision September 24 (#94): neither third-party storage sync nor client-side end-to-end encryption is a parity requirement; Tadooer keeps self-hosted server sync.
rows.acceptance: None; excluded by owner decision.
rows.offlineSync: Self-hosted server sync with the offline outbox (ADR 0010).
